normal: clear and well-defined lung fields with uniform radiolucency
symmetrical lung expansion with no signs of consolidation
sharp and well-outlined diaphragm with normal positioning
costophrenic and cardiophrenic angles are clearly visible
no evidence of increased lung opacity or patchy infiltrates
normal bronchovascular markings without congestion or blurring
absence of pleural effusion, thickening, or fluid accumulation
intact cardiac silhouette with well-defined borders
clear airways with no evidence of bronchial wall thickening
absence of any focal lesions, masses, or alveolar opacities
pneumonia: presence of patchy or diffuse alveolar opacities in one or both lungs
airspace consolidation leading to increased lung density
asymmetrical lung involvement, often localized to one lobe
blurred or indistinct bronchovascular markings due to inflammation
evidence of air bronchograms within consolidated lung areas
irregular or hazy lung borders, indicating inflammatory exudate
possible pleural effusion appearing as fluid accumulation at lung bases
loss of normal diaphragmatic and cardiac silhouette due to opacity
hyperinflation or volume loss in affected lung segments
increased interstitial markings suggesting viral or atypical pneumonia
